title: Arcane Horse Arena: Orb Capture Challenge
description: The player controls a horse on a circular arena, collecting and depositing glowing ShaderBall orbs into scoring zones. Each orb has an elemental type (fire, ice, lightning) and scoring zones only accept matching types. The player must strategically collect, swap carried orbs, and use undo/redo to optimize their route while a conservation law ensures the total energy across all orbs remains constant—powering up one orb drains others.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load horse.glb as the player-controlled character and ShaderBall2.glb to create 6 orb instances scattered on a flat circular arena (radius 20 units). Camera: perspective at (0,25,30) looking at origin. Lighting: ambient light 0.4 intensity plus one directional light casting shadows. The arena is a large cylinder geometry with grid texture. Each ShaderBall2 orb is scaled to 0.4 and tinted one of three colors: red (fire), blue (ice), yellow (lightning). Place 3 scoring pedestals at arena edges, each matching one element color. Player moves the horse with WASD keys with smooth interpolation and rotation toward movement direction. When the horse is within distance 2 of an orb, pressing E picks it up (max carry 2 orbs shown floating above horse). Pressing Q swaps the order of carried orbs (affects which deposits first). Pressing F near a matching pedestal deposits the first carried orb for 100 points. Conservation law: total luminance energy across all 6 orbs is fixed at 600. Pressing R on a carried orb powers it up by 50 (doubles deposit score) but all remaining orbs lose proportional energy and shrink slightly. Orbs below 30 energy shatter and respawn after 8 seconds at base energy, redistributing lost energy equally. Implement full undo (Z key) and redo (X key) supporting up to 20 states—tracking horse position, orb positions, carry state, energy values, and score. Display a HUD with score, carried orbs, energy bar for each orb, and undo/redo stack depth. Add particle effects on deposit and shatter events. The game ends when all 6 orbs have been deposited, showing final score.
